newsitem.title: GERMANY: German plastics processing industry more upbeat.
newsitem.headline: German plastics processing industry more upbeat.

text.p: The German plastics processing industry is slightly more upbeat for the 1997 business year, predicting stronger production and sales growth even though price pressures were seen hurting the industry's results.

Norbert Wagner, head of the industry association Gesamtverband kunststoffverarbeitende Industrie (GKV), told journalists on Wednesday that sales would likely rise by 4.3 percent this year with production climbing by 3.5 percent.
On the other hand, Wagner said about one quarter of all German plastics processing groups would likely swing to losses in 1997 as intense price pressures were sure to impact results.

Referring to former Volkswagen AG purchasing manager Jose Lopez de Arriortua, famous for pushing prices dramatically lower, Wagner said: "One Lopez left the industry, but some 100 little Lopezes have emerged."

But industry association members were slightly more upbeat than Wagner was, as 38 percent predicted improved results this year. This compares with only 24 percent who had predicted improved results for the 1996 business year.
Investments in 1997 were expected to remain at year-ago levels, at around three billion marks, Wagner said.
Suffering under the effects of a soft first quarter last year, the industry posted total sales of around 65.8 billion marks, down 1.6 percent from 1995 levels, the group said.
Wagner explained that a surge in production in the second half of 1996 helped recover some ground lost when production dropped about 8.5 percent during the first quarter 1996.
Prices droppped by only 0.8 percent, he added.
Wagner said the industry had largely completed its downsizing which meant that jobs, reduced by about 8,000 to 270,000 last year, would be secure for some time.
In fact the industry was encountering difficulties in filling available jobs with not all 1,000 trainee positions taken up.
